parole.significato: to abate, to die down, to subside, to let up, to ease off
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Spanish amainar, amaynar (c. 1348), from Old Catalan amainar (whence Catalan amainar), of uncertain origin.

Inherited from Old Spanish angoxa, itself borrowed from Old Catalan angoxa, from Latin angustiae (“tribulations, difficulties”). (/ʃ/ > /x/ is not a native outcome of /-stj-/ in Spanish.) Doublet of angustia. Compare modern Catalan angoixa.
Inherited from Old Spanish carreta, possibly borrowed from Old Catalan carreta, from carro + -eta.
Probably borrowed from Old Catalan coxin~coixin (modern coixí), from Vulgar Latin *coxīnum (“cushion”), from Latin coxa (“hip”). Compare French coussin, Italian cuscino.
Inherited from Old Spanish congoxa, from Old Catalan congoxa, from Late Latin congustia (“defile”, noun).
Borrowed from Old Catalan cortapisa.
Borrowed from Old Catalan escabell, a parallel form to escambell, from Latin scabellum.
From Old Catalan faena (“task, chore”) (modern Catalan feina), from Latin facenda (“things to do”), from faciō. Compare Portuguese faina. Doublet of hacienda.

parole.significato: delicacy, food, sustenance (especially delicious food, or one of the types of foods listed below)
parole.testo: From a verb that originally meant "to eat" (preserved in Portuguese), borrowed from Old Catalan or Occitan or Old Occitan menjar, from Vulgar Latin mandicāre, Latin manducāre. Doublet of manducar and mangar.
From Old Catalan motle with metathesis, from Latin modulus.
From Old Spanish papel, from Old Catalan paper. Doublet of paper.

Most likely borrowed from Old Catalan polvora (first attested in Spanish c. 1350), from older polvera, from Late Latin pŭlvĕra, neuter plural based on Latin pulvis m. Compare French poudre or Old Occitan polvera, poldra, porba. Doublet of polvo < *pulvus.

Borrowed from Old Catalan relotge (1362) (Modern Catalan rellotge), from the older orollotge, from Latin hōrologium, from Ancient Greek ὡρολόγιον (hōrológion). The current form of the word may partly be a back-formation of relojes, plural of obsolete reloje, which better conforms with the Catalan so
Inherited from Old Spanish reptar, probably borrowed from Old Catalan or Old Occitan reptar, inherited from Latin reputāre. Doublet of reputar, a borrowing from Latin.

First attested 1335; borrowed from Old Catalan and Occitan or Old Occitan salvatge, sauvatge, from Vulgar Latin salvāticus, alteration of Latin silvāticus (“wild”, literally “of the woods”), from silva (“forest, grove”). Doublet of selvático.

parole.significato: tailor (person who makes, repairs, or alters clothes professionally)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Spanish sastre, from Old Catalan sastre, from earlier sartre, from Latin sartor.
Borrowed from Old Catalan or Old Occitan semblar.
Inherited from Old Spanish troço, from Old Catalan troç (now tros).

Inherited from Old Spanish trebol, from Old Catalan trèvol (whence modern Catalan trèvol), from Vulgar Latin *trifulus < *trifolum, from Latin trifolium, a calque of Ancient Greek τρίφυλλον (tríphullon, “clover”). Doublet of trifolio. Cognate with English trefoil.

parole.significato: vinegar (a sour liquid formed by the fermentation of alcohol used as a condiment or preservative)
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Spanish vinagre, probably borrowed from Old Catalan vinagre, from Latin vīnum ācre.
Deverbal from zozobrar, or borrowed from Old Catalan sotsobre, from sots + sobre; cf. modern Catalan sotsobrar (“to capsize”).
